data.long_meaning: Goddess Parvati, the divine consort of Lord Shiva. The name Parthavi comes from Parvatam, which means 'mountain' in Sanskrit. Parvati is the goddess of fertility, love, and relationships. She is also known as the giver of life, and her name is believed to bring prosperity and happiness. The name Parthavi carries the meaning “Maiden of the heavens” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Parthavi usually hope their child will grow to embody maiden of the heavens and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine, creativity, and nurturing. Inspires spiritual growth and self-realization.
data.etymology: Parthavi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Maiden of the heavens.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parthavi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Parthavi holds significant importance in Indian culture, as Parvati is one of the most revered goddesses. She is often depicted as a beautiful woman, adorned with flowers, jewels, and other symbolic items. Her stories and legends are a part of Hindu folklore, and she is celebrated during various Hindu festivals such as Karva Chauth and Navratri.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Parthavi holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the divine feminine energy. Parvati is believed to embody the nurturing, loving, and compassionate aspects of the universe. Her name is believed to bring peace, prosperity, and happiness to one's life. For those seeking spiritual growth, the name Parthavi is a reminder of the power of love, devotion, and selflessness in attaining inner peace and connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parthavi, meaning 'belonging to the earth', signifies a deep connection with the physical world and the nurturing, grounding energies of the Earth element. It represents the embodiment of the divine feminine, rooted in the present moment and in harmony with the cycles of nature.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu goddess Parthavi is identified with the goddess of the earth, Prithvi. In Hindu mythology, Prithvi is the wife of the god Brahma and the mother of all creatures. Parthavi is believed to be an aspect of Prithvi, representing the fertile and nurturing aspects of the earth.

Another reference to Parthavi can be found in the Puranic literature where she is mentioned as the daughter of the sage Veda Vyasa and the goddess Satyavati. She is the mother of the great hero Bhishma, who plays a pivotal role in the Mahabharata.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
